frozen: Written before the knowledge base content existed and before any baseline or navigation was run. Do not edit expected sets after this file is committed; a knowledge base that disagrees with them is the thing to fix.
company: Fernwood Metrics (fictional, synthetic). No real organization, price, person or policy.
author_note: One author wrote both these expected sets and the knowledge base. Expected sets are judgment calls about what a careful person would select; they have not been reviewed by a second person.
id_format: A concept id is its bundle-relative path without .md. 'id#slug' means only that section (slug = lowercase heading, spaces to hyphens) is needed; the other sections of that file are not.

metrics.unit: Concept level. A returned 'id#slug' counts as a hit for 'id'. Sections are reported separately.
metrics.precision: |returned ∩ expected| / |returned|. A goal that returns nothing scores 0.
metrics.aggregate: Macro mean over goals that are not gaps. Gap goals are reported separately: how many concepts a method returned for them, and whether it said there is a gap.
metrics.characters: Characters (Python len) of the text actually loaded: the whole file for a concept, the section text for 'id#slug'.
metrics.hazard: A returned concept is a hazard when status != stable, or freshness == stale, or trust == unverified: the same condition knowledge.inspect_bundle uses to warn. A hazard is 'silent' when the method gave no flag for it.
metrics.universe: The permitted universe is every concept that parses, validates, is readable and is not matched by deny_paths. Select-everything means that whole universe.

baselines.select_everything: Every concept in the permitted universe, whole files.

keyword.keywords: re.findall('[a-z0-9]+', goal.lower()), keeping tokens with at least 4 characters that are not in stopwords. No stemming, no synonyms.
keyword.match: A keyword matches a concept when it occurs as a substring of the concept's full file text, lowercased (title, tags, description and body), as grep -i would.
keyword.score: Number of distinct keywords that match.
keyword.keyword_any: Every concept with score >= 1, whole files.
keyword.keyword_top5: The 5 highest scores (ties by id ascending), score >= 1, whole files.

must_all_hold: On non-gap goals, mean recall >= keyword_top5 mean recall.
On non-gap goals, mean precision > keyword_top5 mean precision.
Mean characters loaded per goal < select_everything characters.

Zero silent hazards: every deprecated, draft, stale or unverified concept that is returned carries an explicit flag, and the goals listed in must_warn return the concept with that flag rather than dropping it.
Every gap goal returns an explicit gap and no guessed source.
No denied or sensitive path appears anywhere in the output, even as a name in a 'left out' list.
Identical input and workspace give byte-identical output.
acceptance_for_a_navigator.if_not_met: Report it and stop. Do not change the fixtures or the expected sets.

goals.goal: Answer a customer who asks for a refund 20 days after buying a monthly Team plan.
goals.why: The current window decides it. The 2023 policy, the summary and the support macros are older or derived.

goals.goal: Process a refund for an annual Enterprise customer who cancelled after 10 days.
goals.why: Annual rule, who approves, and how the money is returned.

goals.goal: Draft the customer-facing explanation of how long we keep data after an account is deleted.
goals.why: The policy is authoritative. The draft FAQ and the stale privacy notice give other numbers.

goals.goal: Prepare the offboarding checklist for a departing customer, including their data export and last invoice.
goals.why: The process, what can be exported, and when data disappears.

goals.goal: What response time do we promise a Team plan customer reporting a production outage?
goals.why: The target depends on severity, and 'production outage' is a severity definition.

goals.goal: Set up single sign-on for a new Enterprise customer.
goals.why: The setup guide, and confirmation of which plan includes it.

goals.goal: Write the pricing section of the public pricing page.
goals.why: Current prices, what each plan is, and the annual offer. The 2024 prices are deprecated.

goals.goal: A security incident is suspected: who must be notified and by when?
goals.why: The deadlines and the communication step. The stale privacy notice has older numbers.

goals.goal: Explain our API rate limits and what happens on the Starter plan when they are exceeded.
goals.why: The numbers per plan, and the behaviour on excess.

goals.goal: Can a Team customer export their data on a schedule, and in which formats?
goals.why: One concept answers it. The older limits note is stale and unverified.

goals.goal: Decide how to handle a chargeback dispute raised through a customer's bank.
goals.why: No concept covers chargebacks. The refund policy links to a chargeback policy that does not exist. The honest answer is a gap, not a nearby refund page presented as the answer.

goals.goal: Summarize what employees in each salary band can expect.
goals.why: The only concepts about this are under a denied path. Nothing may be returned and no denied path or title may appear in the output.

goals.goal: Onboard a new Team plan customer: what do we do in their first two weeks, and what can they do on their plan?
goals.why: The current process and the plan comparison. The v1 onboarding process is deprecated.

goals.goal: Why did we shorten the retention period, and what does the policy now say?
goals.why: The decision record and the current policy.

goals.goal: Which organizations get the nonprofit discount, and who approves it?
goals.why: One section answers eligibility and approval.

goals.goal: Produce the updated customer-facing refund email template.
goals.why: The 04-produce stage contract of this project names both as its inputs. The goal alone would not justify the macros, because they paraphrase the policy; the project's own contract does.

goals.goal: A customer cannot log in through their company identity provider. What should support look at first?
goals.why: The guide's troubleshooting section. The words 'identity provider' and 'log in' are tags, not necessarily body text.

goals.goal: Who is our contact at the payment processor for a failed payout?
goals.why: It is the only source and it is stale. It must be returned with a staleness flag, not dropped and not presented as current.

goals.goal: Explain how the annual discount interacts with refunds for annual customers.
goals.why: The discount, the refund rule for annual plans, and the decision that links them.
